inputs.original_text: ISRAEL’S parliament began a debate today on a Bill that would make the death penalty the default punishment for West Bank Palestinians convicted of murdering Israelis. The Bill’s passage would be a victory for Israel’s far-right Minister of National Security Itamar Ben-Gvir, leader of the religious party that introduced the legislation. Opponents of the legislation call it racist, draconian and unlikely to deter attacks by Palestinian militants.
inputs.modified_text: This is being sold as a response to violence, but the real point is to make state power more openly punitive toward Palestinians. A death sentence as the default for Palestinians convicted of murdering Israelis is not some neutral justice measure; it draws a stark line around whose lives the system is prepared to protect and whose it can discard. Ben-Gvir’s party introduced it, and its passage would hand the far-right minister a political victory. The talk of deterrence looks like cover: opponents already warn it is unlikely to stop attacks, while the law could still serve as a warning to Palestinians and a way to normalize harsher control.
